blocks.packageReason: Tier B split by hand (gate: the lethal-hit test; residual: multi-hit memory, Sturdy test, Damp block). Users (4 attrs): Aftermath attr 0, Perish Body attr 1, Unstable Core attr 2 and Pungency attr 1, all `{ power: 100, flinch: true }` with the default Normal type (the dispatcher replaces the vanilla contact-chip attr in place, patchAftermath). All four gates are legacy: the library has no atom for 'the damage of this hit is at least my HP' (request R-B10-c4-03). Package justified: the effect (a) leaves the holder at 1 HP through the Sturdy tag and a direct clamp of later sub-hits, (b) cuts the attacker's multi-hit volley, (c) builds a one-off Explosion-id move with the chosen power, type, always-flinch rider, no contact, all-adjacent targets and a self-KO, and (d) queues it as a FOLLOW_UP move ahead of every other move. Library pieces exist for (a) only (effect.cap-damage), not for (b), (c) or (d), and splitting (a) from the rest would let a rule survive without exploding (request R-B10-c4-08). Typed settings: power, always-flinch, type. Oddities, NOT fixed: the class name says PostFaint but it is a pre-damage clamp; the KO is credited to the explosion, not to the attacker (class comment); a hit that would knock out a holder under a Damp-class ability faints it normally; the explosion category is chosen with getEffectiveStat at the moment of the hit.

blocks.packageReason: Tier C (no gate). Users (2 attrs): Balloon Bomb attr 1 (100 power, no flinch, Normal) and Victory Bomb attr 0 (100 power, no flinch, Fire); nothing to bind. Package justified: a fainted Pokemon cannot run a move phase (MovePhase bails on an inactive user), so the class computes each foe's damage with getAttackDamage for a made-up Explosion-id move and applies it directly; the library 'Use a move' effect needs a real move and a living user, so it cannot be used (request R-B10-c4-09 for a 'hurt every adjacent foe' effect). Typed settings: power, flinch, type. Oddities, NOT fixed: the sibling class of Aftermath (PostFaintDetonateAbAttr) differs in timing, the always-flinch default and reach (that one is a pre-damage clamp that fires on damaging hits only); the class reads simulated only in apply.
